title: Lease-based circuit breaker for SCIM deprovisioning to prevent cascading failures
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: During tenant-wide SCIM churn (e.g., bulk deprovision from IdP or misconfigured group sync), downstream workers that process deprovision events can get overwhelmed, causing cascading retries, duplicate deletions, and noisy audit trails. Existing retry/backoff mechanisms are per-item and do not consider global tenant-level health or operator intent. This leads to spikes in API errors, longer recovery windows, and difficult incident remediation.

Proposed solution: Implement a lease-based circuit breaker layer in the SCIM provisioning pipeline that: (1) acquires a short-lived 'deprovision lease' at tenant or connector scope before executing bulk destructive operations; (2) exposes a tenant-level circuit state (OPEN / HALTING / CLOSED) that gates aggressive retries and escalations; (3) uses adaptive timers and probe-based health-checks to automatically transition state and allow safe resumption; and (4) records structured audit events for each state transition.

Key behaviors: Acquire-lease flow for bulk deprovision: API receives bulk deprovision request -> coordinator attempts to acquire lease; if lease denied, request is queued or fast-failed based on operator config. Circuit states: CLOSED (normal), HALTING (temporarily limit concurrency and switch to safe-mode single-threaded deprovision), OPEN (reject or rate-limit destructive processing). Health probes: small sampled user/group reconciles and IdP heartbeat metrics used to decide transition. Operator controls: admin console toggle to force OPEN/HALTING/CLOSED and per-connector TTL settings.

Why this is different: Instead of only item-level retries, this design adds an operator-observable tenant-scoped control plane that prevents blow-ups during mass changes and produces clearer audit trails for compliance teams.
acceptance_criteria: Lease acquisition and release implemented for tenant and connector scopes
Circuit state persisted in durable store and exposed via internal API
Operator control exists in Console to force and schedule circuit states
Adaptive probe mechanism reduces retry parallelism automatically during HALTING/OPEN
Structured audit events emitted for every lease attempt, acquisition, release, and state transition
E2E integration tests for bulk deprovision, including simulated IdP flapping and slow downstream services
design_notes: Use existing provisioning coordinator service but add a small lease table in CockroachDB keyed by (tenant_id, connector_id)
Lease TTL default 30s with exponential safe-backoff when HALTING is in effect; configurable per-tenant
Circuit transitions driven by a rule engine using metrics: downstream error rate, queue depth, and probe failures
Probe implementation: sample 1% of reconciles as synthetic dry-run deletes to validate downstream health before allowing parallel operations
Audit events should follow existing structured schema: event_type, tenant_id, connector_id, actor, reason, prev_state, new_state, trace_id
implementation_tasks: Coordinator: lease acquire/retry logic and fast-fail paths
Worker: honor circuit state and backoff policies
Console: UI controls to view circuit state and force transitions
Audit: emit structured events and wire into audit-log pipeline
E2E tests and chaos tests simulating IdP bulk deprovision and downstream latency
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: New lease coordination could introduce latency to normal small requests; Mitigation: fast-path for single-user operations that bypass lease if request below threshold
Risk: Incorrect probe criteria may cause unnecessary halts; Mitigation: start with conservative thresholds and feature-flag the adaptive transitions
Risk: Migration for existing long-running operations colliding with new leases; Mitigation: migration script to reconcile active jobs and graceful-suspend long-running jobs during rollout
monitoring_and_metrics: Alert: sustained tenant error rate > 5% for 5m triggers automatic HALTING investigation runbook
Audit dashboard showing state transitions per-tenant with links to trace IDs
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (dev): feature-flagged implementation in staging with synthetic load tests
Phase 2 (canary): enable for 5 pilot tenants, monitor metrics and audit logs for 48h
Phase 3 (gradual): progressive rollout to 25% tenants over 2 weeks with ops on-call
Phase 4 (GA): enable by default with console controls; document runbooks and run a postmortem readiness check
security_considerations: Ensure lease API requires internal auth scope and is not exposed to public tenants
Audit events must include the operator identity when forced transitions are performed
RBAC: only admin roles (org-admin + infra ops) can force circuit state via Console/API
